title: Lists sort with NULL elements lowest; no `<` or `min` on lists
verdict: `list_null_order: LEAST` in sorts; list comparisons refused
description: `sort` orders lists lexicographically, a prefix first, and a NULL element below every value: `[] < [NULL] < [1] < [1, NULL] < [1, 2]` ascending, reversed descending, NULL lists first by default. `<` between lists and `min`, `max` of lists raise (`InvalidOperationError`).
The docs are silent on how lists sort: a docs gap.
No upstream test pins the prefix order; it may change between versions.
reference: `list_null_order`: NULL where a NULL element decides `<`, and `GREATEST` in `ORDER BY` (#207). DuckDB puts the NULL element above every value (duckdb-R11).

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

evidence.note: `list.sort(descending=False, nulls_last=False)` sorts the elements inside each list; it says nothing about how lists compare
`sort(descending, nulls_last)`; no word on list keys

notes: The docs are silent on the order of lists and on `min`/`max` of lists; the rows rest on the 2026-11-04 probes (list-sort, list-compare, list-min).
The docs at `stable` are those of Polars 2.1.0: their [source] links point at tag py-2.1.0.
Streaming gives what in memory gives on every probe and observation cited here.
The observations' frames hold a few rows, which streaming runs as one-row morsels; the probes' 6000-row columns cover morsels of many rows.

`python -m sverify_dev.probe_polars --diff --write` runs each probe one row at a time and on a 6000-row column with `collect(engine='in-memory')` and `collect(engine='streaming')`, and each observation twice: its `df(...)` frame's `select`, `with_columns`, `filter`, `sort`, `unique`, `join` and `group_by` go through the streaming engine the second time (`StreamingFrame`); the `s-` observations collect a lazy query on each engine themselves. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), macOS arm64.

evidence.note: list sort: arg_sort over row-encoded keys
list encoding: continuation token per element, termination token after; prefix sorts first
into_nested: element NULLS_LAST = DESCENDING, so a NULL element is lowest ascending (#22557)
streaming sort row-encodes a list key the same way
